claims.claim: Accumulated CED-1 in trim-21 mutants directly binds to VHA-10.
claims.source: In the absence of TRIM-21, CED-1 accumulated post-translationally and drove cell corpse degradation defects, as evidenced by direct binding to VHA-10.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claims.claim: When C. elegans cells undergo apoptosis, CED-8 activation by CED-3 produces phosphatidylserine (PS) on the cell surface.
claims.source: When Caenorhabditis elegans cells undergo apoptosis, the activation of CED-8 by CED-3 produces phosphatidylserine (PS) on the cell surface, acting as an 'eat-me' signal that is recognized by phagocytes to activate two parallel, redundant genetic pathways (Huang et al., 2012; Suzuki et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claims.claim: Phosphatidylserine on the apoptotic cell surface acts as an 'eat-me' signal recognized by phagocytes.
claims.source: When Caenorhabditis elegans cells undergo apoptosis, the activation of CED-8 by CED-3 produces phosphatidylserine (PS) on the cell surface, acting as an 'eat-me' signal that is recognized by phagocytes to activate two parallel, redundant genetic pathways (Huang et al., 2012; Suzuki et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claims.claim: The ced-2/5/12 pathway mediates activation of the small GTPase CED-10/Rac1 for actin cytoskeleton rearrangement during cell corpse engulfment.
claims.source: The ced-2/5/12 pathway mediates the activation of the small GTPase CED-10/Rac1, leading to rearrangement of the actin cytoskeleton for cell corpse engulfment (Wang et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claims.claim: TTR-52 binds to both exposed PS and the extracellular domain of CED-1, acting as a bridging molecule.
claims.source: In the ced-1/6/7 pathway, TTR-52 binds to both exposed PS and the extracellular domain of CED-1, acting as a bridging molecule to cross-link PS with CED-1 (Wang et al., 2010; Zhou et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claims.claim: CED-7 is a homolog of the mammalian ABC transporter.
claims.source: CED-7, a homolog of the mammalian ABC transporter, functions in both dying and engulfing cells, is required for the enrichment of CED-1 around cell corpses (Mapes et al., 2012; Wu and Horvitz, 1998).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claims.claim: CED-7 functions in both dying and engulfing cells and is required for enrichment of CED-1 around cell corpses.
claims.source: CED-7, a homolog of the mammalian ABC transporter, functions in both dying and engulfing cells, is required for the enrichment of CED-1 around cell corpses (Mapes et al., 2012; Wu and Horvitz, 1998).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claims.claim: CED-6 interacts with the cytoplasmic tail of CED-1 through its phosphotyrosine-binding domain (PTB).
claims.source: After the phagocytic receptor CED-1 recognizes PS, the adaptor protein CED-6 (GULP) interacts with the cytoplasmic tail of CED-1 through its phosphotyrosine-binding domain (PTB) to transduce engulfment signals to downstream effectors (Liu and Hengartner, 1998; Su et al., 2002)
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claims.claim: CED-6 transduces engulfment signals to downstream effectors including DYN-1, clathrin, and clathrin adaptors AP2 or epsin.
claims.source: After the phagocytic receptor CED-1 recognizes PS, the adaptor protein CED-6 (GULP) interacts with the cytoplasmic tail of CED-1 through its phosphotyrosine-binding domain (PTB) to transduce engulfment signals to downstream effectors (Liu and Hengartner, 1998; Su et al., 2002), including the large GTPase dynamin (DYN-1) (Yu et al., 2006), clathrin, and clarithin adaptors AP2 or epsin (Chen et al., 2013; Shen et al., 2013), to promote actin rearrangement for the internalization of ACs.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claims.claim: Phagosomes fuse with lysosomes to form phagolysosomes that digest corpses using lysosomal acid hydrolases.
claims.source: The phagosomes then fuse with lysosomes to form phagolysosomes that digest corpses using lysosomal acid hydrolases (Kinchen et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claims.claim: CED-1 shares sequence similarity with MEGF10 and Jedi in mammals and Draper in Drosophila.
claims.source: CED-1 shares a sequence similarity with several cell surface proteins, including multiple EGF-like domains 10 (MEGF10) (Kay et al., 2012) and Jedi in mammals (Wu et al., 2009) and Draper in Drosophila (Ziegenfuss et al., 2008), all of which have been implicated in the recognition of ACs.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claims.claim: MEGF10, Jedi, and Draper have been implicated in the recognition of apoptotic cells.
claims.source: CED-1 shares a sequence similarity with several cell surface proteins, including multiple EGF-like domains 10 (MEGF10) (Kay et al., 2012) and Jedi in mammals (Wu et al., 2009) and Draper in Drosophila (Ziegenfuss et al., 2008), all of which have been implicated in the recognition of ACs.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claims.claim: The CED-1 receptor is recycled from the phagosome back to the cell membrane by the retromer complex.
claims.source: Our previous work showed that the CED-1 receptor is recycled from the phagosome back to the cell membrane by the retromer complex.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction as previous work by the authors.

claims.claim: Loss of function of the retromer results in lysosomal degradation of CED-1.
claims.source: The recycling of CED-1 by the retromer complex is critical for AC clearance as the loss of function of the retromer results in the lysosomal degradation of CED-1 (Chen et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claims.claim: In Drosophila glial cells, Draper intracellular domain promotes phagocytosis through an ITAM-domain-SFK-Syk-mediated signaling cascade.
claims.source: In Drosophila glial cells, Draper intracellular domain promotes phagocytosis through an ITAM-domain-SFK-Syk-mediated signaling cascade (Ziegenfuss et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claims.claim: The transcriptional factor STAT92e promotes clearance of degenerating axonal debris by directly activating transcriptional expression of Draper.
claims.source: And the transcriptional factor STAT92e promotes the clearance of degenerating axonal debris by directly activating the transcriptional expression of Draper (Musashe et al., 2016; Purice et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claims.claim: The transcriptional factor Serpent is required for sufficient phagocytosis of ACs in Drosophila embryonic macrophages through Draper regulation.
claims.source: Recently, the transcriptional factor Serpent, a GATA factor homolog (Waltzer et al., 2016), was observed to be required for sufficient phagocytosis of ACs in Drosophila embryonic macrophages through the Draper regulation (Kurant et al., 2008; Shlyakhover et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claims.claim: Bfc serves as a Serpent co-factor to upregulate transcription of the engulfment receptor Croquemort in Drosophila macrophages.
claims.source: Our recent study also showed that Bfc serves as a Serpent co-factor to upregulate transcription of the engulfment receptor Croquemort, and thus boosts macrophage efferocytosis in response to excessive apoptosis in Drosophila (Zheng et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claims.claim: Pretreatment of wild-type C. elegans with chloroquine led to a marked increase in endogenous levels of CED-1.
claims.source: We found that pretreatment of wild-type (WT) C. elegans with CQ led to a marked increase in the endogenous levels of CED-1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: CED-1 undergoes lysosome-mediated degradation.
claims.source: These results suggest that although CED-1 is recycled to the cell membrane during phagocytosis of the cell corpse (Chen et al., 2010), the remaining CED-1 still undergoes lysosome-mediated degradation.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the chloroquine treatment results with reference to previous work.

claims.claim: Endogenous CED-1 accumulated to higher levels with increasing doses of MG132 in WT worms.
claims.source: In WT worms pre-treated with different concentrations of the proteasome inhibitor MG132, we observed that endogenous CED-1 accumulated to higher levels with increasing doses of MG132 (Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study shown in Figure 1A.

claims.claim: Endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly increased in uba-1 and ubq-2 RNAi knockdown lines compared to WT controls.
claims.source: We then generated C. elegans RNAi knocked down for either the sole E1 enzyme gene uba-1 or the single-copy ubiquitin gene ubq-2 and found that endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly increased compared to WT controls in both of these transient suppression lines (Figure 1B)
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: The proteasomal pathway is involved in CED-1 degradation.
claims.source: We then generated C. elegans RNAi knocked down for either the sole E1 enzyme gene uba-1 or the single-copy ubiquitin gene ubq-2 and found that endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly increased compared to WT controls in both of these transient suppression lines (Figure 1B), suggesting that the proteasomal pathway was involved in CED-1 degradation.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the RNAi knockdown results.

claims.claim: Endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly increased after treatment with CQ and MG132 overlay compared to CQ or MG132 treatment alone.
claims.source: To examine the relationship between lysosome- and proteasome-dependent CED-1 degradation, we treated C. elegans with CQ and MG132 overlay and found that endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly increased compared to those after CQ or MG132 treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: CED-1 is poly-ubiquitinated in C. elegans.
claims.source: Anti-FLAG immunoprecipitates with antibodies against ubiquitin (Ub) revealed several poly-ubiquitinated forms of CED-1 (Figure 1C), confirming that CED-1 was indeed poly-ubiquitinated in the worms.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: CED-1 acts as a substrate for poly-ubiquitylation and is degraded by the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.
claims.source: These observations confirmed that CED-1 acted as a substrate for poly-ubiquitylation and was degraded by the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ubiquitination and proteasome inhibition experiments.

claims.claim: Inactivation of b0281.8, k01g5.1, and f43c11.7 resulted in accumulation of significantly higher endogenous CED-1 protein levels in all three replicates.
claims.source: We found that the inactivation of three potential E3 ligases, b0281.8, k01g5.1, and f43c11.7, resulted in the accumulation of significantly higher endogenous CED-1 protein levels in all three replicates (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the RNAi screen shown in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: Only b0281.8 interacted with CED-1 in yeast two-hybrid assays among the three E3 ligase candidates.
claims.source: Among these three candidates, only b0281.8 interacted with CED-1 in yeast two-hybrid (Y2H) assays (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the Y2H assays shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: B0281.8 is an ortholog of human TRIM21 containing an N-terminal RING finger domain, a BBox domain, and a C-terminal α-helical coiled-coil domain.
claims.source: The analysis of the B0281.8 sequence showed that this E3 UB-ligase was an ortholog of human TRIM21 containing an N-terminal RING finger domain, a BBox domain, and a C-terminal α-helical coiled-coil domain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B)
claims.evidence: This is a finding from sequence analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B.

claims.claim: Recombinant CED-1 protein was pulled down by GST-TRIM-21 but not by GST.
claims.source: Recombinant CED-1 protein was pulled down by GST-TRIM-21 but not by GST, indicating that TRIM-21 could directly interact with CED-1 (Figure 1F).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: TRIM-21 directly interacts with CED-1 in vitro.
claims.source: Recombinant CED-1 protein was pulled down by GST-TRIM-21 but not by GST, indicating that TRIM-21 could directly interact with CED-1 (Figure 1F).
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the GST pull-down results.

claims.claim: CED-1 was immunoprecipitated from heat shock-treated worm lysates using FLAG antibodies but not from untreated control lysates.
claims.source: To further determine whether TRIM-21 also interacts with CED-1 in vivo, we generated an integrated transgenic strain xwhIs28(Phsp-16trim-21::flag) that expressed a TRIM-21-FLAG fusion protein under the control of a heat shock promoter and found that CED-1 was immunoprecipitated from heat shock-treated worm lysates using FLAG antibodies, but not from untreated control lysates (Figure 1G).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 1G.

claims.claim: TRIM-21 interacts with CED-1 in vivo.
claims.source: These results confirmed that TRIM-21 interacts with CED-1 in vivo.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the co-IP experiments.

claims.claim: The amino acid region between residues 931–1007 in the intracellular domain of CED-1 is sufficient to bind TRIM-21.
claims.source: The results showed that the amino acid region between residues 931–1007 in the intracellular, but not extracellular, domain of CED-1 was sufficient to bind TRIM-21 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F)
claims.evidence: This is a finding from Y2H and GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claims.claim: The coiled-coil domain of TRIM-21 is required for its interaction with CED-1.
claims.source: and the coiled-coil domain of TRIM-21 was required for its interaction with CED-1 (Figure 1H, Figure 1—figure supplement 1G–I).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from Y2H and GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G–I.

claims.claim: TRIM-21 interacted with full-length CED-1 but not with CED-1 variant harboring a C-terminal deletion.
claims.source: Co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) assays using an integrated C. elegans strain smIs34 expressing a full-length CED-1::GFP fusion protein under the native CED-1 promoter and a second integrated transgenic line, smIs110, which expressed a GFP-fused CED-1 with the C-terminal region deleted (CED-1ΔC::GFP), also driven by the native promoter, revealed that TRIM-21 interacted with the full-length CED-1, but not with the CED-1 variant harboring a C-terminal deletion (Figure 1I).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from co-IP assays shown in Figure 1I.

claims.claim: CED-1-TRIM-21 binding is mediated by the interaction between the CED-1 intracellular domain and the TRIM-21 coiled-coil domain.
claims.source: These data demonstrated that CED-1-TRIM-21 binding was mediated by the interaction between the CED-1 intracellular domain and the TRIM-21 coiled-coil domain.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the truncation and co-IP experiments.

claims.claim: hTRIM21 interacts with MEGF10-CT and CED-1-CT.
claims.source: Interestingly, we found that hTRIM21 interacted with MEGF10-CT and CED-1-CT, whereas TRIM-21 interacted with CED-1-CT and MEGF10-CT, suggesting that TRIM-21 is an ancient E3 ligase in which the coiled-coil domain recognizes its substrate CED-1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D and E).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from interaction assays shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D and E.

claims.claim: TRIM-21 is an ancient E3 ligase in which the coiled-coil domain recognizes its substrate CED-1.
claims.source: Interestingly, we found that hTRIM21 interacted with MEGF10-CT and CED-1-CT, whereas TRIM-21 interacted with CED-1-CT and MEGF10-CT, suggesting that TRIM-21 is an ancient E3 ligase in which the coiled-coil domain recognizes its substrate CED-1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D and E).
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the cross-species interaction results.

claims.claim: CED-1 protein accumulated to significantly higher levels in worms carrying the trim-21(xwh12) allele than in those carrying the WT allele.
claims.source: WB analysis indicated that CED-1 protein accumulated to significantly higher levels in worms carrying the trim-21(xwh12) allele than in those carrying the WT allele (Figure 1J)
claims.evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 1J.

claims.claim: The transcription level of CED-1 was unaltered in trim-21(xwh12) mutants.
claims.source: but the transcription level of CED-1 was unaltered (Figure 1K)
claims.evidence: This is a finding from qRT-PCR shown in Figure 1K.

claims.claim: TRIM-21 is required for CED-1 degradation.
claims.source: WB analysis indicated that CED-1 protein accumulated to significantly higher levels in worms carrying the trim-21(xwh12) allele than in those carrying the WT allele (Figure 1J), but the transcription level of CED-1 was unaltered (Figure 1K), which further suggested that TRIM-21 was required for CED-1 degradation.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the Western blot and qRT-PCR results.

claims.claim: Full-length CED-1::GFP in smIs34 and bcIs39 were higher in progeny carrying trim-21(xwh12) than in controls.
claims.source: We observed that full-length CED-1::GFP in smIs34 and bcIs39, but not CED-1ΔC::GFP in smIs110, were higher in the progeny carrying trim-21(xwh12) than in the controls (Figure 1L)
claims.evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 1L.

claims.claim: The CED-1 intracellular domain is required for its binding and degradation by TRIM-21.
claims.source: We observed that full-length CED-1::GFP in smIs34 and bcIs39, but not CED-1ΔC::GFP in smIs110, were higher in the progeny carrying trim-21(xwh12) than in the controls (Figure 1L), which demonstrated that the CED-1 intracellular domain was required for its binding and degradation by TRIM-21.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the Western blot results with different CED-1 constructs.

claims.claim: Endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly higher after vps-37 knockdown in WT worms and trim-21 mutants than in controls.
claims.source: Following knockdown of VPS-37, which blocks lysosomal degradation of CED-1 (Chen et al., 2010), in WT worms and the trim-21 mutant, the endogenous levels of CED-1 were significantly higher than those in the control (Figure 1M and N).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 1M and N.

claims.claim: TRIM-21 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that interacts with CED-1 to mediate its degradation independently of lysosome-dependent degradation of CED-1.
claims.source: Thus, TRIM-21 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that interacted with CED-1 to mediate its degradation independently of lysosome-dependent degradation of CED-1.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the vps-37 knockdown experiments.

claims.claim: Only inactivation of ubc-21 led to increased levels of endogenous CED-1 among 22 E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes tested.
claims.source: We found that only the inactivation of one candidate E2 enzyme, ubc-21, led to the increased levels of endogenous CED-1 (Table 2)
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the E2 enzyme RNAi screen shown in Table 2.

claims.claim: UBC-21 interacts with TRIM-21 in yeast two-hybrid assays.
claims.source: and that UBC-21 apparently interacted with TRIM-21 in Y2H assays (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from Y2H assays shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Recombinant TRIM-21 protein was pulled down by GST-UBC-21 but not by GST alone.
claims.source: GST pull-down assays showed that the recombinant TRIM-21 protein could be pulled down by GST-UBC-21, but not by GST alone (Figure 2B)
claims.evidence: This is a finding from GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: TRIM-21 directly interacts with UBC-21 in vitro.
claims.source: GST pull-down assays showed that the recombinant TRIM-21 protein could be pulled down by GST-UBC-21, but not by GST alone (Figure 2B), indicating that TRIM-21 directly interacted with UBC-21 in vitro.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the GST pull-down results.

claims.claim: The coiled-coil domain of TRIM-21 interacts with UBC-21.
claims.source: Using TRIM-21 truncation constructs in Y2H assays, we further observed that the coiled-coil domain of TRIM-21 interacted with UBC-21 (Figure 2C and D).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from Y2H assays shown in Figure 2C and D.

claims.claim: CED-1-CT was poly-ubiquitinated by purified HA-UBQ-2, UBA-1, UBC-21, and TRIM-21 in vitro.
claims.source: To further investigate whether UBC-21 (E2) and TRIM-21 (E3) catalyzed poly-ubiquitin modification of CED-1, we performed in vitro ubiquitination assays using a CED-1 variant consisting of only the C-terminal intracellular domain (CED-1-CT) and found that it was poly-ubiquitinated by purified HA-UBQ-2, UBA-1, UBC-21, and TRIM-21.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from in vitro ubiquitination assays.

claims.claim: Poly-ubiquitination of CED-1-CT was completely abolished by removal of either UBC-21 or TRIM-21.
claims.source: Notably, poly-ubiquitination of CED-1-CT was completely abolished by the removal of either UBC-21 or TRIM-21 (Figure 2E)
claims.evidence: This is a finding from in vitro ubiquitination assays shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: UBC-21 and TRIM-21 mediate poly-ubiquitination of CED-1-CT in vitro.
claims.source: Notably, poly-ubiquitination of CED-1-CT was completely abolished by the removal of either UBC-21 or TRIM-21 (Figure 2E), indicating that UBC-21 and TRIM-21 mediated the poly-ubiquitination of CED-1-CT in vitro.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the in vitro ubiquitination results.

claims.claim: CED-1 is poly-ubiquitinated in C. elegans in vivo.
claims.source: Antibody detection of HA in immunoprecipitation lysates obtained from the recombinant progeny revealed a smear of high-molecular mass species (Figure 2F), indicating that CED-1 was poly-ubiquitinated in the worms.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: Poly-ubiquitination of CED-1 was greatly reduced in both ubc-21(lf) and trim-21(lf) mutants.
claims.source: We then introduced ced-1::flag and ha::ubq-2 into the ubc-21(xwh15) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) and trim-21(xwh12) knockout strains and found that poly-ubiquitination of CED-1 was greatly reduced in both the ubc-21(lf) and trim-21(lf) mutants (Figure 2F and H).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 2F and H.

claims.claim: K48R- but not K63R-ubiquitin abolished poly-ubiquitination of CED-1-CT in vitro.
claims.source: We found that inclusion of K48R- (conserved function in regulating protein degradation) but not K63R- (signal transduction) ubiquitin abolished poly-ubiquitination of CED-1-CT in vitro (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from in vitro ubiquitination assays shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: K48R- but not K63R-ubiquitin abolished CED-1 poly-ubiquitination in vivo.
claims.source: WB assays to detect ubiquitination of CED-1 by anti-FLAG immunoprecipitation showed that K48R-, but not K63R-, ubiquitin abolished CED-1 poly-ubiquitination in vivo (Figure 2G and H)
claims.evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 2G and H.

claims.claim: CED-1 is modified by K48-linked but not K63-linked poly-ubiquitination.
claims.source: WB assays to detect ubiquitination of CED-1 by anti-FLAG immunoprecipitation showed that K48R-, but not K63R-, ubiquitin abolished CED-1 poly-ubiquitination in vivo (Figure 2G and H), indicating that CED-1 was modified by K48-linked, but not K63-linked poly-ubiquitination.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the ubiquitination assays with different ubiquitin mutants.

claims.claim: Ubiquitination of CED-1 by vps-37 knockdown was similar to that in the control.
claims.source: Ubiquitination of CED-1 by vps-37 knockdown was similar to that in the control (Figure 2I and J)
claims.evidence: This is a finding from co-IP experiments shown in Figure 2I and J.

claims.claim: Lysosomal degradation of CED-1 does not affect poly-ubiquitination of CED-1.
claims.source: Ubiquitination of CED-1 by vps-37 knockdown was similar to that in the control (Figure 2I and J), suggesting that lysosomal degradation of CED-1 does not affect poly-ubiquitination of CED-1.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the vps-37 knockdown ubiquitination results.

claims.claim: UBC-21 and TRIM-21 together catalyze K48-linked poly-ubiquitination of CED-1.
claims.source: Collectively, these observations demonstrated that UBC-21 and TRIM-21 together catalyzed K48-linked poly-ubiquitination of CED-1.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ubiquitination experiments.

claims.claim: CED-1 accumulated at higher levels in ced-3(n717), ced-4(n1162), ced-8(n1891), ced-7(n1892), and ced-6(n1813) mutants, as well as in ttr-52 RNAi-treated worms.
claims.source: The results showed that CED-1 accumulated at higher levels in the ced-3(n717), ced-4(n1162), ced-8(n1891), ced-7(n1892), and ced-6(n1813) mutants, as well as in the ttr-52 RNAi-treated worms (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A)
claims.evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The core cell death machinery, surface-exposed PS on ACs, and CED-7/CED-6 pathways are required for CED-1 degradation.
claims.source: The results showed that CED-1 accumulated at higher levels in the ced-3(n717), ced-4(n1162), ced-8(n1891), ced-7(n1892), and ced-6(n1813) mutants, as well as in the ttr-52 RNAi-treated worms (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), indicating that the core cell death machinery, surface-exposed PS on ACs, and CED-7/CED-6 pathways were required for CED-1 degradation, whereas the ced-2/5/12 pathway was not.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the Western blot results with different mutants.

claims.claim: The ced-2/5/12 pathway is not required for CED-1 degradation.
claims.source: The results showed that CED-1 accumulated at higher levels in the ced-3(n717), ced-4(n1162), ced-8(n1891), ced-7(n1892), and ced-6(n1813) mutants, as well as in the ttr-52 RNAi-treated worms (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), indicating that the core cell death machinery, surface-exposed PS on ACs, and CED-7/CED-6 pathways were required for CED-1 degradation, whereas the ced-2/5/12 pathway was not.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the Western blot results showing no effect of ced-2/5 mutations.

claims.claim: No significant differences in CED-1 levels were observed between control RNAi-treated and dyn-1 or ap-2 RNAi-treated worms.
claims.source: No significant differences in CED-1 levels were observed between control RNAi-treated and dyn-1 or ap-2 RNAi-treated worms (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B)
claims.evidence: This is a finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: CED-6 may perform the last step necessary for CED-1 degradation.

results.result: CED-1 is degraded by both lysosomal and proteasomal pathways. Treatment with chloroquine or MG132 increased CED-1 levels, and combined treatment had additive effects. RNAi knockdown of uba-1 or ubq-2 increased CED-1 levels, and CED-1 was shown to be poly-ubiquitinated in vivo.
results.evaluation: Claims C28-C35 provide converging evidence from pharmacological inhibition (chloroquine, MG132), genetic knockdown (uba-1, ubq-2 RNAi), and biochemical detection (ubiquitination assays) that CED-1 undergoes both lysosomal and proteasomal degradation. The data are internally consistent and use multiple complementary approaches.

results.result: TRIM-21 (b0281.8) is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that directly interacts with CED-1. The interaction occurs through the coiled-coil domain of TRIM-21 and the intracellular domain (residues 931-1007) of CED-1. This interaction is conserved, as human TRIM21 also interacts with both CED-1 and MEGF10.
results.evaluation: Claims C36-C48 demonstrate TRIM-21 identification through RNAi screening (C36), direct interaction via Y2H and GST pull-down assays (C37, C39-C40), co-IP in vivo (C41-C42), and domain mapping (C43-C46). The cross-species conservation data (C47-C48) strengthen the biological significance. Multiple independent assays converge on the same conclusion.

results.result: TRIM-21 is required for CED-1 degradation. In trim-21 mutants, CED-1 protein levels increased without changes in mRNA levels, and the CED-1 intracellular domain was required for TRIM-21-mediated degradation. This degradation pathway is independent of lysosomal degradation.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C55 establish TRIM-21's role in CED-1 degradation through genetic loss-of-function analysis (C49-C51), domain requirement studies (C52-C53), and independence from lysosomal pathways (C54-C55). The combination of protein accumulation without transcriptional changes and domain-specific effects provides strong evidence for post-translational regulation.

results.result: UBC-21 and TRIM-21 together catalyze K48-linked poly-ubiquitination of CED-1. UBC-21 was identified through RNAi screening and shown to interact with TRIM-21 via its coiled-coil domain. In vitro and in vivo ubiquitination assays demonstrated that both UBC-21 and TRIM-21 are required for CED-1 ubiquitination, specifically through K48 linkages.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C71 provide comprehensive evidence for the E2-E3 ubiquitination mechanism. The identification of UBC-21 (C56), demonstration of TRIM-21-UBC-21 interaction (C57-C60), in vitro reconstitution (C61-C63), in vivo validation (C64-C65), and K48-linkage specificity (C66-C68) form a complete mechanistic picture. The independence from lysosomal pathways (C69-C70) is also demonstrated.

results.result: CED-1 degradation requires the core cell death machinery, surface-exposed phosphatidylserine, and the CED-7/CED-6 pathway, but not the ced-2/5/12 pathway. CED-6 function is specifically required for TRIM-21-mediated CED-1 degradation in engulfing cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C78 systematically test genetic requirements using multiple mutants and RNAi. The accumulation of CED-1 in specific pathway mutants (C72-C74), lack of effect from downstream factors (C75-C76), and genetic interaction with TRIM-21 overexpression (C77-C78) establish pathway specificity. The experimental design appropriately tests epistatic relationships.

results.result: CED-6 directly interacts with TRIM-21 and mediates TRIM-21 recruitment to the apoptotic cell surface. The interaction occurs through the PTB domain of CED-6 and the coiled-coil domain of TRIM-21. CED-6 does not serve as a substrate for TRIM-21.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C89 demonstrate CED-6-TRIM-21 interaction through GST pull-down (C79-C80), co-IP (C81-C82), domain mapping (C83-C84), and functional recruitment assays (C86-C89). The lack of CED-6 degradation by TRIM-21 (C85) clarifies the adaptor role. Co-localization studies in ced-6 mutants (C87-C88) provide functional validation of the recruitment mechanism.

results.result: CED-6 binds to the NPXY motif of CED-1 through its PTB domain, and this interaction does not require tyrosine phosphorylation. The N962A mutation in the NPXY motif impairs CED-6 binding, increases CED-1 levels, reduces TRIM-21 binding to CED-1, and decreases CED-1 ubiquitination.
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C100 establish the CED-6-CED-1 interaction mechanism through binding assays (C90-C91), functional rescue experiments (C92-C93), mutagenesis studies (C94-C96), and downstream effects on protein levels and ubiquitination (C97-C99). The data consistently show that CED-6 binding to the NPXY motif is required for TRIM-21-mediated CED-1 degradation (C100).

results.result: SRC-1 is a tyrosine kinase that directly interacts with CED-1 through both its SH2 and SH3 domains. Loss of SRC-1 increases CED-1 levels and reduces CED-1 ubiquitination. SRC-1 does not act specifically within either the ced-1 or ced-2 engulfment pathway.
results.evaluation: Claims C101-C110 identify SRC-1 through RNAi screening (C101), demonstrate direct interaction via multiple assays (C102-C105), and show functional consequences of SRC-1 loss (C106-C108). The genetic interaction studies (C109-C110) appropriately test pathway specificity. The use of CRISPR knockout and multiple binding assays strengthens the conclusions.

results.result: SRC-1 phosphorylates CED-1 at tyrosine 1019 in the YXXL motif. The Y1019F mutation reduces phosphorylation, impairs engulfment function, decreases CED-1 degradation rate, and reduces CED-1 ubiquitination. However, Y1019 phosphorylation is not required for CED-1 binding to CED-6 or TRIM-21.
results.evaluation: Claims C111-C121 identify the phosphorylation site through LC-MS/MS (C111-C112), validate its functional importance through rescue assays (C113-C114), confirm phosphorylation by SRC-1 (C115-C116), and demonstrate effects on protein stability and ubiquitination (C119-C120). The finding that phosphorylation is not required for CED-6/TRIM-21 binding (C117-C118) suggests an alternative pathway, which is addressed in subsequent claims.

results.result: NCK-1 is an SH2 domain-containing adaptor protein that directly interacts with both CED-1 and TRIM-21. NCK-1 is required for CED-1 degradation through the proteasome pathway. The interaction between NCK-1 and CED-1 requires phosphorylation of CED-1 at Y1019.
results.evaluation: Claims C122-C139 identify NCK-1 through RNAi screening (C122), demonstrate direct interactions via multiple assays (C123-C126), show functional consequences of NCK-1 loss (C127-C136), and establish phosphorylation-dependent binding (C137-C138). The use of both RNAi and CRISPR knockout, combined with biochemical and genetic evidence, provides strong support for NCK-1's role as a phosphorylation-dependent adaptor.

results.result: Loss of UBC-21 or TRIM-21 causes accumulation of cell corpses due to defective corpse clearance rather than excessive apoptosis. TRIM-21 is ubiquitously expressed and can be functionally replaced by human TRIM21. UBC-21, TRIM-21, and CED-1 function in the same genetic pathway.
results.evaluation: Claims C140-C154 establish the in vivo function of the ubiquitination machinery through cell corpse counting (C140-C141), cell death analysis (C142), overexpression studies (C143), and rescue experiments (C148-C150). The genetic epistasis analysis (C151-C154) appropriately demonstrates pathway relationships. The functional conservation with human TRIM21 (C149-C150) is particularly significant.

results.result: Loss of UBC-21 or TRIM-21 does not affect recognition and initiation of engulfment but impairs phagosome maturation at a late stage. Specifically, these mutants show reduced association with lysosomal markers (LAAT-1, NUC-1, CPL-1), decreased phagosomal acidification, and delayed chromatin degradation.
results.evaluation: Claims C155-C165 systematically characterize the phagosome maturation defect using multiple markers (C155-C158), acidification assays (C160-C161), and time-lapse imaging (C162-C164). The data consistently show that the defect occurs after engulfment initiation, specifically affecting late-stage phagosome maturation and acidification. The use of multiple independent markers strengthens the conclusion.

results.result: VHA-10, a V-ATPase subunit, directly interacts with CED-1. Loss of vha-10 phenocopies trim-21 mutants, showing increased cell corpses, delayed clearance, and impaired phagosome maturation and acidification. Overexpression of VHA-10 rescues the trim-21 mutant phenotype, indicating that VHA-10 dysfunction causes the cell corpse degradation defects in trim-21 mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C166-C176 identify VHA-10 through LC-MS/MS (C166), confirm direct interaction (C167), demonstrate phenotypic similarity (C168-C173), establish genetic pathway relationship (C170-C171), and provide functional rescue (C174-C176). The rescue experiment (C174-C175) is particularly strong evidence that VHA-10 dysfunction is responsible for the trim-21 phenotype. The mechanistic link between CED-1 accumulation and VHA-10 inhibition is well-supported.

results.result: CED-1 recycling is normal in trim-21 mutants, and CED-1 levels on membranes are comparable to wild-type. However, co-localization and interaction between CED-1 and VHA-10 are dramatically increased in trim-21 mutants. Excess CED-1 in trim-21 mutants binds VHA-10, negatively affecting phagosomal acidification and blocking cell corpse degradation.
results.evaluation: Claims C177-C184 distinguish the trim-21 phenotype from retromer-mediated recycling defects (C177-C179), demonstrate increased CED-1-VHA-10 interaction in trim-21 mutants (C180-C182), and provide a mechanistic explanation for the phagosome maturation defect (C183-C184). The comparison with snx-1 mutants is particularly informative, showing that the mechanisms are distinct. The data support the model that excessive CED-1 inhibits VHA-10 function.

results.result: TRIM-21-mediated proteasomal degradation of CED-1 occurs independently of lysosomal degradation through the retromer complex.
results.evaluation: Claims C185 and C55 (which are essentially the same conclusion stated in different sections) are supported by the vps-37 knockdown experiments showing that blocking lysosomal degradation does not prevent the effects of TRIM-21 on CED-1 levels. This establishes two parallel degradation pathways for CED-1.

results.result: Background information on apoptotic cell clearance pathways in C. elegans and related organisms, including the roles of phosphatidylserine signaling, the ced-1/6/7 and ced-2/5/12 pathways, CED-1 homologs, and transcriptional regulation of engulfment receptors.
results.evaluation: Claims C11-C27 provide established background knowledge from the literature, appropriately cited. These claims set the context for the current study but do not represent new findings. They are well-supported by the cited references and accurately represent prior knowledge in the field.
